title: Graphs form an open subfunctor of the Hilbert functor for algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces and morphisms as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For morphisms of algebraic spaces, flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite presentation means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness (the diagonal is quasi-compact); quasi-compact means that inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. A closed immersion of spaces is a representable morphism whose scheme base changes are closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale charts, and universally closed means closed on underlying topological spaces after every algebraic-space base change [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $Z\to B$ and $W\to B$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$, with $Z\to B$ proper, flat and of finite presentation and $W\to B$ separated. Put $Z_T=Z\times_BT$ and $W_T=W\times_BT$ for a scheme $T\to B$. Let $\mathcal H(T)$ consist of closed subspaces $D\subset Z_T\times_TW_T$ proper, flat and of finite presentation over $T$, with inverse-image transition maps. The graphs $\Gamma_f=(\mathrm{id},f)$ define a natural injective transformation $\gamma:(T\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_T(Z_T,W_T))\to\mathcal H$. For every scheme $T\to B$ and $D\in\mathcal H(T)$, there is an open subscheme $V_D\subset T$ such that for every $T'\to T$, the projection $D_{T'}\to Z_{T'}$ is an isomorphism if and only if $T'\to T$ factors through $V_D$. Under the injection $\gamma_{T'}$, the family $D_{T'}$ belongs to the image exactly when this projection is an isomorphism; in that case the unique associated morphism is $\operatorname{pr}_2|_{D_{T'}}\circ(\operatorname{pr}_1|_{D_{T'}})^{-1}$. Equivalently, $h_T\times_{\mathcal H}\operatorname{Mor}_B(Z,W)\simeq h_{V_D}$, where $h_T(T')=\operatorname{Hom}_B(T',T)$ and $\operatorname{Mor}_B(Z,W)(T')=\operatorname{Hom}_{T'}(Z_{T'},W_{T'})$. Thus the image of $\gamma$ is an open subfunctor of $\mathcal H$: its inverse image on every scheme test is an open subscheme. No finite-presentation assumption is imposed on $W\to B$.

proof.text: For every scheme $T\to B$, [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] gives that $Z_T\to T$ is proper, flat and of finite presentation. By [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition], $W_T\to T$ is separated. The same permanence statement applies to every family $D\to T$ in $\mathcal H(T)$ after every $T'\to T$. Thus their structural morphisms remain proper, flat and of finite presentation.

Representable closed immersions remain closed immersions under algebraic-space base change: a scheme test of the new map is a scheme test of the old map, so the required represented scheme and its closed immersion are already supplied by the definition in the statement. For $f:Z_T\to W_T$, the square with left map $(\mathrm{id},f):Z_T\to Z_T\times_TW_T$, right map $\Delta_{W_T/T}:W_T\to W_T\times_TW_T$, bottom map $(f\operatorname{pr}_1,\operatorname{pr}_2)$, and top map $f$ is cartesian: its pairs satisfy $f(z)=w$, so $z\mapsto(z,f(z))$ is the inverse parametrization. The fibre-product universal property is [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Since $W_T\to T$ is separated, its diagonal is a representable closed immersion. Hence the graph is closed. As a space over $T$ this closed family is $Z_T$, so Step 1 supplies all three Hilbert conditions. The same closed-immersion base-change argument and Step 1 show that the transition maps preserve $\mathcal H$.

source.place: Tag 0D1A, quot-lemma-Mor-into-Hilb, graph paragraph; explicit cartesian-square argument of spaces-morphisms-lemma-semi-diagonal.

proof.text: The graph construction commutes with every base change. Indeed, after pulling back to $T'$ the graph map has projections $\mathrm{id}_{Z_{T'}}$ and $f_{T'}$, so it equals $(\mathrm{id},f_{T'})$ by the fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Its represented closed subobject is therefore the graph of $f_{T'}$. For identity or composite base changes the same argument compares their two projections and gives the required equality. This proves naturality of $\gamma$.

source.place: Tag 0D1A, natural transformation; explicit fibre-product verification.

proof.text: For a closed family $j:D\hookrightarrow Z_T\times_TW_T$, write $k=\operatorname{pr}_1j$ and $l=\operatorname{pr}_2j$. If $k$ is invertible, set $f=l k^{-1}$. Then $(\mathrm{id},f)k$ has projections $k,l$, hence equals $j$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The isomorphism $k$ identifies the closed subobject $D$ with the graph of $f$. Conversely the first projection of a graph has inverse its graph parametrization. Thus the image criterion is exactly that $k$ is invertible, and its inverse image is uniquely $l k^{-1}$. In particular equal graph subobjects recover equal morphisms, proving injectivity. This argument applies after every base change.

source.place: Tags 0D1A and 0D1B, recovery of a morphism from its graph.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-universal-isomorphism-open] to $A=D$, $C=Z_T$, base $T$ and $f=k$. Its hypotheses on $D\to T$ hold because $D$ is a Hilbert family: finite presentation includes local finite presentation, and properness includes universal closedness. For $Z_T\to T$, Step 1 gives properness, which includes separatedness, finite type (hence local finite type) and universal closedness (hence closedness for the identity base change). These meanings are exactly [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. All six hypotheses hold, without any finite-presentation condition on $W\to B$. The lemma supplies an open subspace of $T$, represented by an open subscheme $V_D\subseteq T$, and its universal condition gives $k_{T'}$ invertible exactly when $T'\to T$ factors through $V_D$.

On a scheme $T'\to B$, a point of $h_T\times_{\mathcal H}\operatorname{Mor}_B(Z,W)$ is a pair $(h,f)$ with $h:T'\to T$ and $\Gamma_f=D_{T'}$. Step 4 says there is exactly one such $f$ if $k_{T'}$ is invertible and none otherwise. Step 5 identifies this condition with a factorization $h:T'\to V_D\hookrightarrow T$, which is unique because an open subscheme inclusion is a monomorphism [def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus the inverse bijections send $(h,f)$ to its factorization and send a factorization to $(h,l_{T'}k_{T'}^{-1})$. Pullback preserves inverse maps: pulling back $kk^{-1}=1$ and $k^{-1}k=1$ shows that the pulled-back inverse is the inverse of $k_{T'}$. Together with Step 3 this proves naturality of both bijections. Therefore the displayed pullback functor is $h_{V_D}$ over $h_T$, as claimed.

source.place: Tag 0D1B, final sentence: explicit functor pullback and natural bijections.
